style_suffix: Quiet documentary still-life photograph inside a lived-in older home in Flanders, shot on 35mm film with a 50mm lens, Kodak Portra 160 colour, soft overcast north-window morning daylight, pale sage green, oatmeal linen, warm oak, terracotta clay and faded blue enamel tones, matte real materials with honest wear, fine organic film grain, gentle low contrast, calm and tender, slightly imperfect framing, no people, no faces, no hands, absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no words, no logos, no labels, no signage, no screens.

jobs.subject: A worn oak kitchen table pushed against a window with sheer linen curtains in the morning: an open spiral notebook with blank cream pages and a pencil, a pair of tortoiseshell reading glasses, a stoneware cup of coffee with warm milk, a weekly pill organiser with plain unmarked lids, a small glass jar of rosemary, a folded wool cardigan over the chair back; the left third of the frame is calm open table and soft light.

An old bedside table in the evening under a small fabric lamp with a warm glow: a plain unlabeled dropper bottle, a glass of water, a folded handkerchief, an analogue wristwatch with a plain dial without numerals lying face up, a crocheted doily, the rest of the room in soft blue dusk shadow.

A lightweight grey rollator walker parked inside a narrow tiled hallway next to the front door, a knitted wool scarf in sage green draped over its handle, a cotton shopping bag hanging from it, a doormat and a coat stand with a beige raincoat, soft daylight falling through the frosted glass of the door.

Overhead view of a loose pile of old photographic prints lying face down showing only their pale backs, tied loosely with a faded ribbon, next to an open shoebox, a magnifying glass and a cup of tea on a linen tablecloth with a small floral embroidery.

A small closed wooden keepsake box with brass corners on an oak sideboard, an old iron key lying beside it on a folded linen cloth, a sprig of dried lavender, soft side light from a window, quiet negative space to the right.

A front door seen from inside a modest home, slightly ajar onto a grey Flemish street in drizzle, an umbrella dripping in a stoneware stand, a bunch of tulips wrapped in brown paper resting on a small hall table with a bowl of keys.

The same oak kitchen table by the window in late afternoon light: the spiral notebook now closed with a pencil on top, an empty cup, the reading glasses folded, a bowl of clementines, long warm shadows across the table, the right third of the frame calm and empty.
